::: {#rem-contrapositive-template}
#### The shape of a proof by contrapositive

A proof by contrapositive (@def-proof-by-contrapositive) of "if $P$, then $Q$" has this shape:

> | Suppose $\neg Q$.
> | $\vdots$
> | Therefore $\neg P$.

Use it when $\neg Q$ gives you more to work with than $P$ does.
In @exr-sum-odd, $\neg Q$ was the equation $x = y$,
while $P$ said only that $x + y$ is odd.

:::
